value.rationale: Positive maps are often used precisely because ordinary fixed-point iteration respects feasibility or order. The theorem isolates the exact two-dimensional coupling threshold at which the squared stage loses that property and shows that the standard adaptive SqS3 norm-ratio choice generically triggers a sign-changing mode even arbitrarily close to the Perron ray. This gives a mathematically motivated boundary for when projection, clipping, or feasibility-aware acceptance is structurally necessary rather than a numerical accident.
